models.purpose: Score which player is performing better without letting the server decide it.
models.summary: Serve win rates p1 and p2 are combined into M1, read as player 1 ahead when above one half. A point window and a time window both move. AUC averages the time-window score over window lengths so that neither a short nor a long window has to be chosen. The printed formula (2) is scrambled.

models.purpose: Test whether points scored by a fixed server are independent draws.
models.summary: Under H0 a fixed server makes points i.i.d. binomial. Ljung-Box on the first match gives p = 0.497 up to 10 lags. The runs test gives P = 0.691. Neither rejects at 0.05 for most matches. Instantaneous win rates rise by about one percent.

models.purpose: Predict the points a player should win from rank alone, so the remainder can be called momentum.
models.summary: Relative rank among the 32 Wimbledon players becomes an expected losing round, six minus log base two of rank. A logistic of the round gap plus a server bonus is the point probability. Newton on 31 matches gives lambda 0.0624 and s 0.1742. Momentum is the points won minus the points this model expects. The word likelyhood is printed.

models.purpose: Predict the residual from short and long windows, with latent state carried between them.
models.summary: Two stacked blocks. The long block aggregates points 40 to 10 back and predicts the next 10. The short block aggregates the last 10 and predicts the next 10. Latent variables are physiology, perception of control, and self-efficacy. Physiology is dropped after a random forest. EM trains six latent variables. A player-1 bias of about 53 against 47 is removed by reweighting, not by mirroring. Importance is the entropy reduction.
